contents.name: Definition 37. A coherent 2-group is skeletal
contents.reason: The carrier directly constructs a skeletal finite model and does not develop the general underlying-category definition of skeletal coherent 2-groups.

contents.name: Definition 38. A special 2-group
contents.reason: The general coherent categorical unit/counit interface is not developed by the finite cochain definition, which specifies its own object and morphism data directly.

contents.name: Proposition 39. Every coherent 2-group is equivalent in C2G to a special 2-group
contents.reason: Reduction of arbitrary coherent 2-groups to chosen skeletons is not needed: the owned claim begins with finite skeletal quadruple data and asserts no equivalence for arbitrary categories.

contents.name: Lemma 40. If C is a coherent 2-group ...
contents.reason: Transport of an arbitrary coherent structure across chosen tensor-product isomorphisms is a categorical equivalence lemma, not a prerequisite for the explicit fixed finite model.

contents.name: Theorem 43
contents.scope: The first bullet supplies the special-2-group quadruple interface, restricted locally to finite groups. The biequivalence and the other bullets classifying arbitrary homomorphisms and 2-homomorphisms are not claimed. The pentagon-to-cocycle equation is written and checked locally; no classification theorem is used as an unproved logical premise.

contents.name: Definition 41. A special homomorphism
contents.reason: The local gauge arrows are explicitly defined vertex and edge labels on a fixed complex; they are not a general theory of monoidal functors between special 2-groups.

contents.name: Proposition 42. Any homomorphism between special 2-groups is isomorphic in C2G to a special homomorphism
contents.reason: Normalizing arbitrary monoidal functors is outside this fixed-background gauge consistency statement; its general categorical isomorphism is not invoked in the local proof.

contents.name: Corollary 44
contents.reason: Classification of all coherent 2-groups up to categorical equivalence is broader than representative change for a fixed finite group/action; no such classification is asserted here.

contents.name: Proposition 45. Every coherent 2-group is equivalent in C2G to a strict one
contents.reason: Strictification by changing the categorical model is outside the owned finite cochain model, which deliberately retains a potentially nontrivial associator.
